sentences.text: Researchers developed a laboratory test using cell cultures from the dorsal root ganglion and microglia to investigate signals that trigger immune cell movement. When these ganglion cells were grown together with microglia, the immune cells migrated more than usual, indicating that the ganglion cells released attracting signals.

The substance ATP, present in the signals released by the dorsal root ganglion, strongly encouraged microglia migration, whereas common pain-related chemicals like CGRP, substance P, and glutamate did not cause movement at normal levels. Two different drugs designed to block ATP receptors worked differently, with one only partially stopping the movement while the other had no effect.
The authors conclude that this new laboratory method provides a useful way to study how nerve cells and immune cells communicate in both healthy and sick states.
